speech.text: Pandas are actually herbivores, right? Um, nope. So why do they eat bamboo? For decades, scientists watched them chew bamboo all day and basically assumed you are what you eat. But if you apply that exact same logic to other animals we know well, you run into trouble right away. Dogs sometimes eat grass to make themselves throw up and polar bears occasionally snack on berries and seaweed when they can't find seals. Does that make them herbivores? Of course not. So scientists actually took a hard look inside a panda's gut. They realized it looks exactly like the gut of a brown bear, a pure carnivore. So if their gut never changed, why did a carnivore switch completely to bamboo? Well, about 4 .2 million years ago, panda ancestors had a genetic mutation that made them lose their taste for meat. And guess what? Bamboo was everywhere. Just like that, pandas fully switched to bamboo. But their digestive system didn't agree. As a result, they only absorb about 17 % of the nutrients, forcing them to eat for 16 straight hours a day just to have enough energy to eat more bamboo.
